Therefore, dear representative of the workers, I'd like to tell you that you're dealing here with someone who knows the House well, understands the challenges facing the House, and We're not talking about a last minute candidate because we had a change in government in my country on June 28th of this year. Because it wasn't possible with the previous government, when the new government took office, then my candidacy was submitted and we followed all of the relevant procedures. Therefore, even before thinking about DG, I can tell you that 10 years ago, I was concerned about all of these same subjects that you have just raised. In other words, thinking about how we could guarantee livelihoods for families and decent work. Thank you very much.
Thank you very much. I turn to Kathleen one last time for the final question from the workers. Kathleen.

Final question of the afternoon. Mr. Gonzalez, over the years, there have been growing concerns over business models that are focusing on preserving shareholders' value and their profit at the expense of decent working conditions for workers. In light of your experience in senior positions on the business side and in government, what role do you see for the ILO to promote a business model that recognises the responsibility of business including through due diligence along the supply chain, and contributes to realizing decent work. What are, in your view, the key challenges to overcome and the key priority actions the ILO should take in addressing them? And how would you rally support from especially employers and businesses at national and international level for such actions? Thank you very much.
Thank you, Kathleen. Sir.

Allow me to begin by thanking you. You referred to my experience. You've referred to my experience as part of the public sector in Peru. I've also been in the business environment, and I'd like to say that in my experience and While I was working for the ILO, I was appreciated by my colleagues, including workers, because I brought their concerns about their working conditions to the attention of the authorities. And I did this. I represented workers, passing on information to the administration, bringing to light their concerns. Whether there was a complaint put down in writing or not, I did this. And I can tell you that we got a good outcome as a result. Now, with regard to the role of businesses, I would like to think that it might be possible that we can go back to what was it year 2000 I don't remember the exact year when there was a global business pact for inclusion something along those lines and we were requested to provide training in a number of countries a global compact or something that was the name of it something like that I was a director in Mexico Cuba and Haiti And in the timeframe of one year, and you can look this up, we trained a few, 100 companies and brought them up to speed on this. And this was also the case in Argentina. And I can tell you that this was a challenge. And I'm proud that we rose to this challenge. Also, in Argentina, we had this business compact, which had a very clear reference to social conditions. Therefore, why would we go about reinventing the wheel? If these experiences met with success, then we can repeat them. And I would like to say that from October through to November, I will be working on updating these mechanisms and processes. Thank you very much.

Thank you very much and thank you to the workers. So, colleagues, we've now completed the question and answer part of the interview. Mr. Gonzalez, Olesya Franco, I'd now like to invite you to make your concluding remarks. You have up to five minutes. The floor is yours.

Thank you very much, Chair. The first thing I would like to say is as follows. I feel blessed and very fortunate to be here. It's a privilege that you have put all of these questions to me. and even some of my responses, I did not offer you sufficient clarity. Please let me know. Send me an e-mail. I am completely available to you. And if you need an answer, I will give it to you. And if I don't have the answer, I will go and study in order to be able to give you an answer to your questions. Because we can't leave anything hanging. I would like to talk about here a kind of intellectual integrity. And I would like to commit to this kind of intellectual integrity. In the remaining seconds or minutes that I have because I understand that the time is actually being counted. I'm keeping my eye on that. But there are two or three points I'd like to make. 37. Okay. That's the time I've already spoken. Okay. This transition is unprecedented. We're talking about a transition and huge changes. It's not the fourth industrial revolution. That's incorrect because the key thing here is artificial intelligence. Now, we're lucky in that we've got a social angle on this. However, that this is an old paradigm from homo sapiens who can do more with less and in this case what they're going to be doing is they're going to achieve more with less employment. So this should be of concern to everyone. We're talking about a kind of social Darwinism here. And I've been very fortunate in life. I've had opportunities to study and to have a wonderful family. My wife, Patricia, is present here listening to me. Therefore, I am very proud and very fortunate. But we cannot live isolated on an island. You cannot isolate yourself with a clear conscience. Knowing, and the speaker's speech is to French, that just 100 meters away, just around the corner, there are many people who are finding new opportunities.

And they really don't find it in this world.

And they also aren't getting any response from the ILO. And that's why I'm saying I am well familiar with the ILO. And I know I've provided some specific responses to questions, and I think I've been clear. But no, I am not going to offer you continuity. No, that's not what I want to do, not more of the same. I want to offer you a qualitative approach that will bring benefits for the organization. I would like to work according to the original mandate because it's a fantastic mandate that this organization had at its inception. And what we want to do is to strive to achieve social justice. And then we can avoid conflicts. We can do that. That is a possibility. However, to achieve that, we need a different kind of organization to lend a helping hand to the office because the director general has to work together with all of you. And at the same time, however, the DG can offer guidance to point towards these changes that we need. Thank you.

Well, thank you very much, Mr. Gonzalez, Alicia Franco, for sharing your vision for the future of the ILO and for taking part in this exercise. So, colleagues, this brings us to the end of today's public interactive event with candidates for the post of DG of the ILO. I really want to thank all of them. all three of them for their sense of global service and contribution. That's not something that we should take for granted at all, especially given the shaky reality of multilateralism and multilateral institutions today.
